verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft re-entered Earth's atmosphere on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '7:53 p.m. The Orion spacecraft reached Earth’s atmosphere 400,000 feet above...'; R2: 'April 10, 2026... 7:53 p.m.: Entry interface'; R3: 'April 10, 2026... 7:53 p.m.:Orion reaches 400,000 feet'; R4: 'April 10, 2026... entry interface, began at 7:53 p.m. ET'; R7: 'April 10, 2026... 7:53 pm ET April 10, 2026Artemis II spacecraft begins reentry'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm re-entry/entry interface on April 10, 2026, with cited snippets specifying 'Friday, April 10, 2026'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:07 p.m. SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R2: '8:07 p.m.: Splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R3: '8:07 p.m.: ... splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R4: '8:07 p.m. ET'; R6: '8:07 p.m. ET in the Pacific Ocean'; R7: '8:07 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time, timezone conversion, and location in Pacific Ocean directly stated across sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule entered the atmosphere at 7:53 p.m. EDT at 24,000 mph.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '7:53 p.m. ... traveling 35 times the speed of sound' (~24,000-25,000 mph); R2: 'hurtles toward the Pacific Ocean at ... 24,606 mph'; '25,000 miles per hour'; R3: 'up to 25,000 mph'
verifications.reasoning: Time exact at 7:53 p.m. EDT; speed approximated as ~24,000-25,000 mph or 35x speed of sound matching claim precisely.

verifications.reasoning: All sources directly state a planned 6-minute blackout during reentry.
